minutes.headline: Budget Task Force ranked its 20 recommendations, putting town account consolidation first and the split tax rate last.
minutes.summary: At its final meeting the Budget Task Force approved prior minutes by roll call, discussed whether to pursue the Community Preservation Act (CPA), and then ranked all recommendations for its executive summary. Priorities were set mostly by consensus, with a targeted diagnostic audit, prudent investor rule, CPA review and HVAC grants near the top. Members also discussed the Medicaid reimbursement data discrepancy, posting the documents, and presentations to the Select Board and Finance Committee.

votes.motion: Approve the prior meeting minutes (roll call vote).

budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed the likely CPA yield as six figures at most, accumulating over years, dependent on state match.
Changing how the town warrant is delivered was estimated to save a small amount; it would also move health insurance rate deadlines earlier.
Carter described a similar consolidation raising yield on a large cash flow, worth a substantial amount per year; it was set as a top priority.

budget_items.topic: Prudent investor rule and consolidation values
budget_items.what_was_said: The written recommendations estimated ranges for prudent investor rule and consolidation.
Phase two grant application awaits a decision in spring; potential grant value is large and recurring across phases.
figures_as_heard: three quers of a million dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Subsidy on the recycling side of trash/recycling was discussed as a possible six-figure saving if the town left the business.
Raised that a notable free cash increase makes this year a good time to request funds for the targeted diagnostic; an RFQ subject to appropriation was suggested to get a figure.

budget_items.topic: Miscellaneous non-recurring revenue and Medicaid reimbursement
budget_items.what_was_said: A drop in miscellaneous revenue was explained by one-time bond premium and supplemental tax; DLS data on Medicaid reimbursement looked inaccurate.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance buyouts and high deductible plan
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussed as ranked recommendations needing PEC input.

decisions.decision: Recommendation number two was split into two items: prudent investor rule and investment/account consolidation.
Top ranking set: consolidate town accounts first, targeted diagnostic audit second, prudent investor rule third, CPA review fourth, split tax rate last.

Final ordering read out of 20 recommendations (e.g. HVAC grants fifth, school and landfill solar sixth and seventh, trash review ninth, Chapter 90 tenth); duplicate title for items 16 and 17 to be fixed.
Task force documents and data slide deck to be posted on the town's budget task force web page and possibly the district site.
Executive summary to be sent before noon the next day; the same update to be presented at Select Board and Finance Committee, and slides sent to Chris Menard after the Select Board.
CPA to stay on the list of potential recommendations in the report.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force ranked its recommendations for its executive summary, putting consolidation of town accounts first and the split tax rate last.
A targeted diagnostic audit, the prudent investor rule and a review of the Community Preservation Act (CPA) were set second through fourth.
The final order of 20 recommendations was read out, with HVAC grants fifth and school and landfill solar sixth and seventh.
The CPA was kept on the list of potential recommendations in the report, after members discussed its likely yield.
The executive summary is due before noon the next day, to be presented to the Select Board and Finance Committee, with the task force's documents and slides to be posted online.

why_it_matters: The ranking sets the order in which the Select Board and Finance Committee will see the task force's proposals, so it shapes which ideas for the town and school budgets get attention first.
A targeted diagnostic audit and the CPA review could each reach a future Town Meeting vote, and the CPA would add a local surcharge to tax bills if adopted.
